examples.en: Unauthorized buildings can be torn down.
It was an unlicensed shop, so it got caught in a crackdown.
If you do business without a license, you have to pay a fine.

examples.ko: 무허가 약을 사지 말라고 뉴스에서 말했어요.
examples.en: The news said not to buy unapproved medicine.
I heard this neighborhood used to have many unauthorized houses.

examples.ko: 무허가 노점상도 있고 허가받은 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some street vendors are unlicensed and some are licensed.

explain: 반대말은 '허가'예요. '무허가 건물', '무허가 영업'처럼 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸미는 경우가 많아요. 일상 대화에서는 '허가 없이'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Unlicensed business is illegal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허가 없이 장사하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for doing business without a license.

phrases.en: You must not open a shop without a permit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무허가로' 뒤에 동사를 붙이면 허가 없이 했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '무허가로' plus a verb means doing it without a permit.

phrases.example: 허가 없이 이곳에 들어가면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not enter here without permission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이렇게 풀어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people spell it out like this.

explain_en: Lacking official permit, for buildings or shops (무허가 건물) Its counterpart is '허가' (permission). It usually modifies a noun, as in '무허가 건물' (unauthorized building) or '무허가 영업' (unlicensed business). In daily talk people may also say '허가 없이' (without permission).

t90.ax: Unauthorized buildings can be torn down.

en: to carry in; to bring in

examples.en: You must not bring drinks into the library.

examples.ko: 공항에서 큰 가방을 반입할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I could not bring the big bag in at the airport.
Please do not bring dangerous items in.
The guests brought in a cake and held a party.

examples.ko: 외부 음식을 반입하려면 미리 말해야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to bring in outside food, you have to say so in advance.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 과일을 반입하는 것을 검사해요.
examples.en: That country inspects the fruit people bring in.

explain: 허락이 필요하거나 검사를 받는 곳에 물건을 들일 때 써요. 규칙 문구에서 '반입하지 마세요'처럼 많이 보여요. 장 본 물건을 집에 들일 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: May I bring this bag inside?
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락을 구할 때 쓰는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A question used to ask for permission.

phrases.en: Please do not bring alcohol into the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙 문구에서 자주 보이는 부정 명령 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative request often seen in written rules.

phrases.en: You must not bring food in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '반입하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday substitute for 반입하다.

explain_en: Use it for bringing things into places that need permission or inspection. It is common in rule notices, like 반입하지 마세요. You do not use it for bringing groceries home.

en: to come into effect; to be effective

examples.en: The new law takes effect next month.
The contract came into force on the day it was signed.
Once the agreement takes effect, tariffs will go down.

examples.ko: 경보가 발효되는 동안에는 밖에 나가지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go outside while the warning is in effect.
This rule is set to take effect at midnight tomorrow.
A heat advisory went into effect, so we canceled the event.

explain: 발효되다는 법, 조약, 경보처럼 공식적인 것이 효력을 갖기 시작할 때 써요. 같은 소리의 '발효'는 김치나 된장이 익는 것도 가리키니 문장에서 구별하세요. '시행되다'는 실제로 실행되는 것에, 발효되다는 효력이 생기는 순간에 가까워요.

phrases.en: The new rule is scheduled to take effect tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 효력이 생길 일을 알릴 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form for announcing something that will take effect.

phrases.en: A typhoon warning has been issued.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경보나 주의보가 공식적으로 내려질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for warnings officially coming into force.

phrases.en: The contract takes effect once you sign.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발효되다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way to say '발효되다'.

explain_en: 발효되다 is used when something official such as a law, treaty or warning starts to have effect. The same-sounding 발효 also means fermentation of kimchi or soybean paste, so tell them apart by context. 시행되다 stresses actual enforcement, while 발효되다 stresses the moment it becomes valid.

t90.ax: The new law takes effect next month.

examples.ko: 그런 시대착오적 발상은 이제 통하지 않아요.
examples.en: That kind of outdated idea doesn't work anymore.
Many people say we should change the outdated rules.

examples.ko: 아직도 그렇게 하는 건 너무 시대착오적이에요.
examples.en: Still doing it that way is way out of touch.

examples.ko: 시대착오적으로 들릴 수 있지만 저는 편지가 좋아요.
examples.en: It may sound old-fashioned, but I like letters.
The ad that was criticized as outdated has been taken down.

examples.ko: 교복 규정이 시대착오적이라고 느끼는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students feel the school uniform rules are outdated.

explain: '시대착오적 발상'처럼 명사 앞에 바로 쓰기도 하고, '시대착오적인', '시대착오적이다'처럼 '이다'를 붙여 쓰기도 해요. 시대에 맞지 않는 생각이나 제도를 비판하는 말이라 뉴스나 토론에서 자주 보여요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '낡았다'나 '구시대적이다'도 써요.

phrases.en: This rule is far too outdated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 서술어로 쓰며, 시대에 뒤떨어졌다고 비판해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 이다 as a predicate, it criticizes something as behind the times.

phrases.en: Outdated thinking needs to change now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 바로 붙여 낡은 생각을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed directly before a noun to describe outdated thinking.

phrases.en: The policy was criticized as anachronistic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 토론에서 비판을 전할 때 '-라는 비판'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: In news and debates, -라는 비판 is added to report the criticism.

explain_en: It can sit directly before a noun, as in '시대착오적 발상', or take 이다, as in '시대착오적인' and '시대착오적이다'. It criticizes ideas or systems that don't fit the times and is common in news and debates. In lighter talk, '낡았다' or '구시대적이다' are also used.

en: to be established; to be newly created

examples.en: A new library is being set up in our neighborhood.
A new department was established at the university this year.

examples.ko: 신설되는 지하철 노선이 우리 집 근처를 지나가요.
examples.en: The newly built subway line passes near my house.
An AI team was set up at the company, so I applied.

examples.ko: 버스 정류장이 신설되면 출근이 훨씬 편해질 거예요.
examples.en: If a new bus stop is set up, commuting will be much easier.
It's a newly established school, so all the buildings are clean.

explain: 학교, 학과, 부서, 노선처럼 조직이나 제도, 시설이 새로 만들어질 때 써요. 물건을 만들 때는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 '설립되다'는 회사나 학교를 처음 세울 때, '신설되다'는 있던 곳에 새로 하나 더 생길 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I use the newly created bus route.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 '새로 생긴 ~'라고 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to mean 'newly created ~'.

phrases.en: I applied to a newly established department this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 생긴 학과를 가리키는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for a newly opened department.

phrases.en: A subway station is scheduled to be built next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 새로 생긴다는 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a plan for something to be newly created.

explain_en: Passive; newly added — departments, schools, rules. Used when an organization, system or facility, such as a school, department, bus route or office, is newly created. It isn't used for making objects. 설립되다 is for founding a company or school from scratch, while 신설되다 also covers a new one being added to what already exists.

dis.h: newly set up; departments, schools, rules
gh: formulated or founded; plans, policies, governments
opened for use; accounts, courses, branches

p.n: 설립되다 is the usual word for founding; 신설되다 stresses that it is newly set up.

t90.ax: The newly built subway line passes near my house.

examples.en: Photography is strictly prohibited inside the museum.
'No entry' is written in large letters on the door.

examples.ko: 시험 중 휴대폰 사용은 엄금이니까 조심하세요.
examples.en: Using a phone during the exam is strictly forbidden, so be careful.
We saw the 'No fishing' sign and turned back.

examples.ko: 여기는 쓰레기 투기 엄금이라서 벌금이 있어요.
examples.en: Dumping trash is strictly banned here, so there's a fine.

examples.ko: 엄금 표시가 있는 곳에는 들어가지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go into places with a strict prohibition sign.

explain: '촬영 엄금', '출입 엄금'처럼 팻말이나 안내문에서 '~ 엄금' 꼴로 자주 보여요. '금지'보다 강하게 절대 하지 말라는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '절대 안 돼요'라고 하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: At the gas station, a sign says 'Smoking strictly prohibited.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 곳의 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on signs at dangerous places.

phrases.en: Bringing phones into the exam room is strictly forbidden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 가지고 들어오지 말라는 안내에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on notices against bringing items inside.

phrases.en: Parking is prohibited in this area.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄금'보다 약한 일반적인 금지 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general ban, weaker than 엄금.

explain_en: You often see it on signs and notices in the form '~ 엄금', like '촬영 엄금' or '출입 엄금'. It feels stronger than '금지', meaning 'absolutely not allowed'. In speech, people more often say '절대 안 돼요'.

en: to be strict; to be rigid; to be impartial

examples.en: The judging must be strict for everyone to trust the result.
The judge ruled on the case strictly.
The exam supervision was strict, so there was no cheating.
We selected the applicants with strict standards.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 성적 처리가 아주 엄정해요.
examples.en: That teacher is very strict in handling grades.
An evaluation that isn't strict leads to complaints.

explain: 심사, 수사, 평가, 판단처럼 공정함이 중요한 일에 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 부모님이나 선생님의 성격이 무섭고 엄격하다고 할 때는 '엄하다'나 '엄격하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서는 '엄정하게 처리하다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The winner was chosen after a strict, fair review.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙는 형태로, 공정하고 엄격한 평가를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun for a review that is both fair and strict.

phrases.en: The police said they would handle the case strictly and fairly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 들리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing you hear most often in the news.

phrases.example: 평가가 엄정하지 않으면 사람들이 결과를 믿지 않아요.
phrases.en: If the evaluation isn't strict and fair, people won't trust the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공정하지 못하거나 느슨하다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for something lax or not impartial.

explain_en: Strict and fair; judging, examination, law; formal. It is a formal word for matters where fairness is important, such as judging, investigation, evaluation and decisions. To say a parent's or teacher's personality is stern, '엄하다' or '엄격하다' sounds more natural. In the news you often hear '엄정하게 처리하다' (handle strictly).

t90.ax: The judge ruled on the case strictly.

examples.ko: 교통 규칙이 위반된 경우에는 벌금을 내요.
examples.en: If traffic rules are broken, you pay a fine.

examples.ko: 계약 조건이 위반되면 취소할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the terms are violated, it can be canceled.
I felt the promise had been broken, so I got angry.
This behavior goes against school rules.
Please check so the law isn't violated.

examples.ko: 그 광고는 규정에 위반될 수 있어요.
examples.en: That ad may violate the regulations.

explain: 법·규칙·약속이 지켜지지 않았다는 결과를 말할 때 써요. '규칙을 위반하다'는 사람이 어긴 것, '규칙이 위반되다'는 규칙 쪽에서 본 표현이에요. 쉽게 말하면 '어기다'이고, 반대말은 '지키다', '준수하다'예요.

phrases.en: This plan does not violate the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 법을 어기지 않았다고 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to confirm that a rule or law has not been broken.

phrases.en: You must not run a red light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때는 '위반하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '위반하다' when a person is the subject.

phrases.en: You shouldn't break a promise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위반하다'보다 쉬운 말이고 약속·규칙에 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that works for promises and rules alike.

explain_en: Describes the result when a law, rule or promise is not kept. '규칙을 위반하다' is the person breaking it; '규칙이 위반되다' looks from the rule's side. The everyday verb is '어기다', and the opposites are '지키다' and '준수하다'.

en: to be nominal; to be name only

examples.en: That rule is practically meaningless now.
Even if a law exists, it becomes a dead letter if nobody follows it.
It's a club in name only, so there are almost no meetings.

examples.ko: 회장은 있지만 하는 일이 없어서 유명무실하다고 해요.
examples.en: There is a president, but he does nothing, so people say it's a title in name only.

examples.ko: 이 제도가 유명무실하게 되지 않으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this system doesn't end up existing in name only.

examples.ko: 그 모임은 몇 년 전부터 유명무실했어요.
examples.en: That group has existed in name only for several years.

explain: 제도, 규칙, 모임처럼 있어야 할 역할을 못 하는 것에 많이 써요. '유명무실해지다'처럼 변화를 나타내기도 하고, 일상 대화에서는 '이름뿐이다', '있으나 마나예요'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: We need to fix the system that exists in name only.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명무실하다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로 바꿔 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used before a noun to describe it.

phrases.en: As members left, the club gradually became a name only.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 역할을 하던 것이 점점 힘을 잃는 변화를 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a change where something gradually loses its function.

phrases.example: 이 우산은 구멍이 나서 있으나 마나예요.
phrases.en: This umbrella has holes, so it's as good as useless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유명무실해요' 대신 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say something is useless in practice.

explain_en: It is often used for systems, rules and groups that no longer do the job they should. You can also say '유명무실해지다' for the change, and in casual talk people say '이름뿐이다' or '있으나 마나예요'.

examples.en: I verify myself with the number I got by text.
The government certified this product.
To log in, verify first.
There is an event where you prove it with a photo.
It takes time to authenticate the app.
I post exercise photos as proof.

explain: 인터넷에서 본인 확인을 할 때 '본인 인증'이라고 많이 말해요. '인증샷'은 갔다는 걸 증명하는 사진을 뜻하는 한국어 말이에요. 제품에 '인증 마크'가 붙기도 해요.

phrases.en: This product received a safety certification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인증하는 쪽이 아니라 인증을 받는 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the one receiving certification.

phrases.en: Please verify your identity with your phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 사이트에서 자주 보는 부탁 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request often seen in apps and websites.

phrases.en: I take a proof photo at a famous restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갔다는 것을 보여 주는 사진을 말하는 한국어 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Korean term for a photo that proves you were there.

explain_en: Online, identity checks are usually called by the noun phrase for self-verification. A Korean term for a proof photo is also built on this word. Products may carry a certification mark.

examples.ko: 회사는 규정을 어긴 직원에게 중징계를 내렸어요.
examples.en: The company imposed a heavy disciplinary action on the employee who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 중징계가 내려지자 선수의 팬들이 크게 아쉬워했어요.
examples.en: When the heavy sanction was handed down, the player's fans were very disappointed.

examples.ko: 학교는 중징계 여부를 다음 주에 결정한대요.
examples.en: The school will decide next week whether to impose a heavy sanction.

examples.ko: 가벼운 실수라서 중징계까지는 필요 없다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people think a heavy sanction isn't needed since it was a minor mistake.

examples.ko: 중징계 소식에 그 공무원은 사과문을 올렸어요.
examples.en: After the news of the heavy sanction, the official posted an apology.

examples.ko: 경징계와 중징계는 처벌의 무게가 완전히 달라요.
examples.en: Light and heavy disciplinary actions differ completely in severity.

explain: 반대말은 '경징계'예요. 기사나 인사 규정에서 '중징계를 받다/내리다/요구하다'처럼 나오고, 정직이나 해임처럼 무거운 처분을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 그 직원은 규정을 어겨서 중징계를 받았어요.
phrases.en: That employee received a severe disciplinary action for breaking the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처분을 받는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when the person receiving the punishment is the subject.

phrases.en: Citizens demanded heavy discipline for the player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 처분을 내려 달라고 할 때 기사에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news when calling for a harsh punishment.

phrases.example: 회사는 두 사람에게 중징계 처분을 내렸어요.
phrases.en: The company handed down severe disciplinary measures to the two people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사 규정이나 공식 문서에서 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression used in personnel rules and official documents.

explain_en: Its opposite is '경징계' (light disciplinary action). In news and personnel rules it appears as '중징계를 받다/내리다/요구하다', and refers to heavy measures such as suspension or dismissal.

examples.en: The company disciplined the employee who broke the rules.
The school decided to discipline that student.

examples.ko: 선수를 징계하는 일은 팀에도 부담이 돼요.
examples.en: Disciplining a player is a burden for the team too.

examples.ko: 잘못을 숨기면 더 크게 징계할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you hide your mistake, they can discipline you more severely.
After the committee imposed the discipline, it announced the result.

examples.ko: 부정행위를 하면 학교에서 징계한다는 안내문이 붙었어요.
examples.en: A notice was posted saying the school will discipline anyone who cheats.

explain: 회사, 학교, 협회 같은 조직이 규칙을 어긴 사람에게 공식적으로 벌을 줄 때 써요. 부모가 아이를 혼내는 일에는 쓰지 않고 '혼내다', '야단치다'를 써요. 보통 '징계를 받다', '징계 처분' 같은 명사 표현으로 더 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 그 직원은 규칙을 어겨서 징계를 받았어요.
phrases.en: That employee was disciplined for breaking the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌을 받는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person who is punished.

phrases.example: 학교가 그 학생에게 징계 처분을 내렸어요.
phrases.en: The school handed down a disciplinary action against the student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 정해진 벌을 말하는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for an officially decided punishment.

phrases.en: The disciplinary committee meets tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌을 정하는 공식 모임 이름으로 회사와 학교에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the official group that decides punishments at companies and schools.

explain_en: Official discipline by schools, companies, or organizations for rule violations. It is for an organization such as a company, school or league officially punishing someone who broke the rules. For a parent scolding a child, Koreans say 혼내다 or 야단치다 instead. You will hear it more often in noun phrases like 징계를 받다 (be disciplined) and 징계 처분 (disciplinary action).

t90.ax: The school decided to discipline that student.

en: to permit; to allow; to approve

examples.en: City Hall approved the construction.
My parents allowed me to go out.
You can't enter unless it's permitted.
This park permits taking photos.

examples.ko: 관리자가 허가한 사람만 문을 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only the people the manager has permitted can open the door.
I'll let you know tomorrow whether we'll permit it.

explain: 관청이나 윗사람이 해도 된다고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. '허락'은 개인 사이에서 더 자연스러워요. 친구에게는 '해도 돼'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: You need to get permission to take photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허가를 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it from the side of the person who receives permission.

phrases.en: My parents allowed me to go on the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인 사이에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural between individuals.

phrases.example: 여기에서 일할 수 있게 허가해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please give permission for me to work here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관청이나 윗사람에게 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask an office or a superior politely.

explain_en: Official permission given when someone asks (외출 허가) Use it when an authority or superior officially says yes. '허락' sounds more natural between individuals. With a friend you would simply say '해도 돼'.

gh: let something be allowed; tolerate it

p.n: 허가 is an official approval; 허용 is a general allowance.

t90.ax: My parents allowed me to go out.

en: being current; being existing; in force

examples.ko: 현행 규칙으로는 이 일을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Under the current rules, we can't do this.
Many people say we should change the current system.
According to the current law, this is illegal.

examples.ko: 현행 방식은 시간이 너무 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: The present method takes too long.
The current rates stay the same until next month.
The school explained the existing regulations to the students.

explain: '지금 쓰이고 있는'이라는 뜻으로 법·제도·규칙·요금 앞에 붙여 써요. '현재'는 시간 전반에 쓰지만 '현행'은 이렇게 제도 앞에 쓰는 말이에요. 사람이나 날씨에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: It can't be stopped under current law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 효력이 있는 법을 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for the law currently in force.

phrases.example: 현행 요금은 한 달에 만 원이에요.
phrases.en: The current rate is 10,000 won a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 내고 있는 요금을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the rate currently being charged.

phrases.en: Please apply according to the current regulations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 공지에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in notices and announcements.

explain_en: Laws, rules or systems currently in effect (현행법) It goes before words like law, system, rule or fee to mean 'the one in use now'. 현재 can describe time in general, but 현행 is used for systems and rules. It is not used for people or weather.

en: to keep; to store; to safekeep

examples.ko: 중요한 서류는 잘 간수해 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to keep important documents safe.

examples.ko: 여권은 잃어버리지 않게 가방 깊숙이 간수했어요.
examples.en: I stored my passport deep in my bag so I wouldn't lose it.

examples.ko: 귀한 물건이라서 아이 손이 닿지 않게 간수해요.
examples.en: It's a precious item, so I keep it out of the children's reach.

examples.ko: 통장을 어디에 간수했는지 기억이 안 나요.
examples.en: I can't remember where I put my bankbook for safekeeping.
Grandmother kept her money in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 비싼 카메라니까 여행 중에도 잘 간수하세요.
examples.en: It's an expensive camera, so keep it safe during the trip too.

explain: '보관하다'와 비슷하지만, 잃어버리거나 상하지 않게 조심해서 잘 둔다는 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 '잘 챙기다', '보관하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '간수하다'는 어른들이 하는 말처럼 들릴 때가 있어요.

phrases.en: Keep your password note safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-세요'를 붙여 조심해서 두라고 부탁하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to keep something carefully.

phrases.en: Did you make sure to bring your passport?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '간수하다' 대신 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요. 물건을 빠뜨리지 않고 가지고 다닌다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word often used instead of '간수하다'; it stresses not forgetting to take or keep something.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep track of; to make sure to bring

phrases.example: 영수증은 한 달 동안 보관해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please keep the receipt for a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 어딘가에 두는 것에 초점이 있어서 더 넓게 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on storing something somewhere, so it is used more widely.

explain_en: Store valuables or documents carefully so they are not lost. It is close to '보관하다' (to store), but it stresses putting something carefully so it won't be lost or damaged. In daily speech '잘 챙기다' or '보관하다' are more common, and '간수하다' can sound like something an older person would say.

dis.h: look after valuables so nothing's lost

p.n: 보관하다 is storing; 간수하다 stresses looking after it so it isn't lost.

t90.ax: It's best to keep important documents safe.
